title: The $3.5 million settlement that extended Comcast’s cable franchise

beats.text: San Francisco’s cable auditor found that access grants were paid late.

visual.sub: The City and the cable operator disagreed on what counted as revenue

beats.text: The operator agreed to $50,589 in interest.

visual.kicker: The City and the cable operator disagreed on what counted as revenue

beats.text: In 2005, the Board voted six to five on a broader Comcast settlement.

visual.kicker: A six-to-five vote linked a settlement with four more franchise years

beats.text: The deal linked $3.5 million to a four-year franchise extension.
The City budgeted that money as one-time revenue.

visual.kicker: A six-to-five vote linked a settlement with four more franchise years

beats.text: The extension replaced a 48-month rebuild deadline with new milestones.

visual.kicker: The extension replaced a 48-month deadline and created two different remedies

beats.text: Certain missed targets could trigger a monthly credit of four dollars per affected subscriber.

visual.kicker: The extension replaced a 48-month deadline and created two different remedies

beats.text: A separate remedy capped specified City damages at $60,000 a month.
The 2007 audit verified the fees paid and still found unresolved revenue questions.

visual.kicker: Auditors continued to question the revenue definition after the deal

beats.text: Those included payments from new channels and advertising commissions.

visual.kicker: Auditors continued to question the revenue definition after the deal

beats.text: Comcast moved to a state franchise in 2008.

visual.kicker: The local and state franchises covered different periods

beats.text: The audits verify fees. The closeout records would show whether anyone received rebuild credits.
